papers.title: Three-dimensional direct laser writing inspired by stimulated-emission-depletion microscopy
reviewed: Author manuscript pp. 6–7: apparatus description; p. 7 Fig. 2: calculated excitation/depletion focal distributions. Fig. 2 is not an optical-train drawing.
opticalTrain: Mai Tai HP excitation, approximately 810 nm
532 nm continuous-wave depletion laser and synchronized AOM
Central 180° phase mask imaged onto the objective entrance pupil
papers.mechanism: A central phase step in the depletion pupil produces axial and radial inhibition around the excitation volume. This is not simply a lateral doughnut.
papers.modelLimits: No stimulated depletion, vectorial PSF, triplet dynamics or resin kinetics are simulated. The 2D meridional phase-zone proxy converts pupil area to diameter but cannot calculate the axial/radial depletion focus. Combiner placement is inferred from the stated common objective, not a published mechanical drawing.
unknowns: Excitation repetition rate and pulse duration are not specified in the retrieved manuscript.
Depletion 50 mW is before the objective; ordinary excitation 7.4–8.3 mW is not a single fixed source power.
Central mask occupies 50% of the pupil area; the native meridional proxy uses the corresponding sqrt(0.5) diameter, while the physical pupil diameter and relay prescription remain unspecified.
papers.summary: Combine excitation and a phase-shaped second beam at one objective.

experiments.control: Excitation / depletion sources and AOM duty
experiments.result: Disable either color or vary AOM duty from 1–99%. The arrival inset distinguishes excitation and CW light; no depletion chemistry is calculated.
Change the central phase zone. The optical path changes while the geometric focus stays fixed.
Switch between static and ±50 µm transverse motion. The fixed micrometer view shows actual ray arrivals and the reported 100 µm/s translation rate.

papers.title: Fabrication of microscale medical devices by two-photon polymerization with multiple foci via a spatial light modulator
reviewed: PDF pp. 6–7, Fig. 1 on p. 7; fabrication examples pp. 8–10.
opticalTrain: Chameleon: 780 nm, <150 fs, 80 MHz; 4 W source specification
Reflective LC-R2500 SLM with tiled CGH
Fourier-plane order selection; zero order removed at plane P
papers.mechanism: The SLM generates multiple independently located foci; the galvos move that pattern. The representative Venus array uses 4×4 foci, with 8–12 mW per spot and 1 mm/s scanning.
papers.modelLimits: No CGH calculation, diffraction efficiency or 3D multi-focus field is solved. The 150 fs value is an upper bound and is deliberately not exported as an exact pulse duration.
unknowns: Relay distances and lens focal lengths are not all specified.
4 W source output is not 8–12 mW per-focus writing power.

Fig. 1 labels the attenuator as a half-wave plate/polarizer and the source as <140 fs; prose describes a liquid-crystal modulator/PBS and <150 fs. The drawing follows the prose and retains this discrepancy.
papers.auxiliaryPath: A CMOS camera branch connects near the scanner; transmission illumination is below the specimen. No APD is specified in Fig. 1.
papers.summary: Create representative focus rows from the full SLM aperture, then scan them.

experiments.result: Disable emission to remove all writing arrivals.
Change the separate geometric-order count. The displayed phase frame is illustrative; it does not calculate the orders or carrier.
Move the focus pattern with a scanner or disturb the relay to see why pupil conjugacy matters.

papers.title: Rapid, continuous projection multi-photon 3D printing enabled by spatiotemporal focusing of femtosecond pulses
reviewed: PDF p. 2 Fig. 1; p. 9 Materials and methods, including observation path omitted from Fig. 1.
opticalTrain: Spitfire amplifier: 800 nm, 65 fs, 5 kHz, approximately 22 nm bandwidth
L1=100 mm and L2=150 mm expansion
DLP3000 DMD, approximately 24° incidence; up to 4 kHz masks
L3=300 mm collecting diffracted light along the DMD normal
papers.mechanism: Stage-synchronized image masks and continuous Z translation remove interlayer dead time. The dispersive DMD and objective establish a temporal focus at the projected image plane.
papers.modelLimits: Discrete 2D frames supply one sampled column to the geometric tracer; a separate carrier supplies wavelength angles. No temporal field, dose, curing or stage/frame synchronization is calculated.
unknowns: 5 kHz is outside the lab repetition-rate range.
Total operating source power is not a single value.
Objective transmission of 70% is a reported assumption. The native objective EFL and WD are design choices.
papers.auxiliaryPath: 50:50 beam splitter before the objective feeds a CCD. A 633 nm alignment laser enters through a DMLP650 dichroic. A GaP detector is used upstream of the DMD while minimizing pulse duration. The compact native view omits the 633 nm alignment/DMLP650 branch and GaP detector, and traces incident light to the CCD rather than a calculated specimen image.
papers.summary: Project changing mask slices and compare wavelength paths at the sample.

experiments.result: Disable emission to remove the projected writing light.
Step through discrete 2D slices; the tracer follows the displayed sampled column.
Move the resin away from its conjugate image plane and inspect the spread of sampled wavelengths. Temporal confinement is not calculated.

papers.title: Ultrafast 3D nanofabrication via digital holography
reviewed: Main PDF p. 2 Fig. 1 and system description; p. 3 Fig. 2 single-pulse results; supplement pp. 2–5 Methods, p. 8 Table S1, p. 12 Fig. S1, and p. 15 Fig. S4/Note 2 nonlinear coefficients.
opticalTrain: Spitfire Pro: 800 nm, 100 fs, 1 kHz, 4 W
L1=225 mm and L2=250 mm dispersion compensation relay
DLP6500 DMD: 1920×1080, 7.56 µm pitch, laser synchronized
Nikon 40× NA 1.3 oil objective, WD 0.24 mm
papers.mechanism: Binary holographic foci can write with one amplified pulse. The authors analyze high-order nonlinear response, rather than assuming a calibrated pure two-photon reaction.
papers.modelLimits: The native scene traces an 800nm central carrier only, not broadband dispersion compensation. The 2D binary frame gates a sampled column; separate geometric orders illustrate focus placement. No CGH optimization, single-pulse initiation, high-order response or dose is calculated.
unknowns: Supplement compensation prose swaps the L1/L2 values; the drawing follows the explicit Fig. S1 caption (225/250 mm).
4 W is source output; reported 5 nJ per focus at 1 kHz is not source power.
papers.auxiliaryPath: 589 nm fibre LED below the substrate reflects from M1 through the objective and dichroic to L6=100 mm and CCD. This observation branch is omitted from the compact native writing view.
papers.summary: Use separately configured angular orders to illustrate random-access focus placement.

experiments.result: Disable the pulsed source or set power to zero to remove every writing arrival.
Change from the default three orders to one or eight. The binary frame and separate geometric orders are configured independently; no hologram is solved.
Steer the pattern or reduce the Fourier filter gap from 16 to 4 mm to select orders; compare actual arrivals and the true pupil footprint.

papers.title: 3D nanolithography with metalens arrays and spatially adaptive illumination
reviewed: OSTI-hosted complete author manuscript pp. 5–7 and 18–20; Extended Data Figs. 1–3 on pp. 25–27; official supplementary PDF pp. 3–6, 12–15 and 22.
opticalTrain: Solstice femtosecond amplifier: 800 nm, 1 kHz, 35 fs, 7 W average output
HWP1/PBS1 power control and −100 mm/+250 mm Galilean beam expander
PBS2/QWP1/reflective LC-SLM double pass: phase-to-amplitude modulation
L1/L2 conjugate relay with vacuum cell around the intermediate focus: 200:200 mm for ML1 or 75:200 mm for ML2
Metalens array directly focuses into resist
Substrate and translation stage above metalens array
papers.mechanism: A spatially varying amplitude pattern illuminates independent metalenses. The metalenses make the foci; the SLM does not generate them as a holographic angular fan. Two benchmark points correspond to 50×50 NA 1 lenses and 370×350 NA 0.8 lenses.
papers.modelLimits: No vectorial high-NA metalens field, spatially adaptive dose, meta-atom efficiency or vacuum propagation nonlinearities are solved. Only representative lenslets fit a 2D view.
unknowns: The version-of-record PDF remains subscription content; apparatus values were verified in the complete OSTI author manuscript.
7 W is total amplifier output, not sample-plane or per-focus power, and is outside the companion lab range.
Metalens focal lengths and most free-space distances are not numerically specified.
The caption names HWP1–2, but the Methods writing-path description specifies HWP1 only and the second HWP is not unambiguously located.
papers.auxiliaryPath: A separate observation objective above the substrate connects to a beam splitter, LED, L3 and CMOS. It is not the writing objective.
papers.summary: Image an intensity mask onto separate lenslets that make the writing foci.

experiments.result: Disable emission or set source power to zero to remove writing arrivals.
Enable individual sampled regions to select independent metalenses.
Move the geometric focus away from the resin and inspect the actual arrival spread.

introduction.title: Basic Two-Photon Polymerization
reviewed: Paper-independent paraxial design. Both scanner pivots are conjugate to the objective back focal plane. All operating values and lens choices are illustrative.
opticalTrain: X galvo, 1:1 inter-pivot relay, Y galvo
Photoresist on an axially moving stage
introduction.mechanism: A focused pulse supplies a localized two-photon excitation region. Pupil-conjugate mirrors move its geometric focus while the stage changes sample depth. The two scanner axes are projected onto this single optical section.
introduction.summary: Follow one pulse train through attenuation, scanning, focusing and sample motion.
introduction.modelLimits: The ray-arrival inset displays actual traced support at the sample. It is not a PSF, voxel, dose or polymerization calculation.
unknowns: All configured values are educational design choices, not a fabrication prescription.

experiments.result: Switch off the pulse train or set power to zero to remove arrivals. Positive source power is metadata; relative attenuation is controlled by the polarization optics.
Change either mirror angle and inspect the shifted sample arrival while the beam stays centered in the pupil.
Play the Z motion to see defocus spread, or shift the pupil relay to produce pupil walk.
